days.title: Amami Oshima

days.title: Yakushima
days.summary: Ancient cedar trees, some more than a thousand years old and one estimated at over seven thousand, stand deep in this UNESCO World Heritage rainforest, the same moss-draped landscape that inspired Hayao Miyazaki's Princess Mononoke.

days.title: Akita
days.summary: Rice paddies and sake breweries define this quiet northern prefecture, its Namahage folklore, fearsome straw-clad demons who visit homes each New Year's Eve to scold lazy children, is unique to the Oga Peninsula and unlike anything else in Japan.

days.title: Kanazawa

days.title: Toba

days.title: Osaka

days.title: Osaka
days.summary: Dotonbori's canal-side neon and giant mechanical crab signs set the tone for a city that treats eating out as a genuine pastime, kuidaore, or eating until you drop, is practically the local motto.
days.label: Until late evening

days.title: Takamatsu
days.summary: Ritsurin Garden, laid out over more than a century for the local feudal lords, is widely considered one of Japan's finest, its ponds and pine-covered hills designed to reveal a new view at every turn.
days.label: Early morning to afternoon

days.title: Shimonoseki
days.summary: Fugu, the potentially lethal pufferfish prepared only by licensed chefs, is close to a civic obsession in this strait-side city, credited with popularizing the delicacy across Japan.
days.label: Early morning to afternoon

days.title: Jeju
days.summary: A volcanic island UNESCO has recognized three times over, for its lava tubes, its crater cone and its overall natural heritage, Jeju rises to Hallasan, South Korea's tallest peak, at its center.
days.label: Early morning to afternoon

days.title: Nagasaki
days.summary: One of the only Japanese ports open to the outside world during the country's two centuries of self-imposed isolation, Nagasaki absorbed Dutch, Portuguese and Chinese influence long before the rest of Japan did, still visible in Glover Garden's colonial mansions and the historic Chinatown quarter.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Fukue
days.summary: The largest of the Goto Islands hides one of Japan's most poignant hidden histories, Christian communities driven underground by centuries of persecution built secret churches and shrines across these islands, several now recognized by UNESCO.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Yakushima
days.summary: Ancient cedar trees, some more than a thousand years old and one estimated at over seven thousand, stand deep in this UNESCO World Heritage rainforest, the same moss-draped landscape that inspired Hayao Miyazaki's Princess Mononoke.
days.label: Morning to late evening

days.title: Amami Oshima
days.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage subtropical rainforest covers much of this Ryukyu island, home to the Amami rabbit, a primitive, dark-furred species found nowhere else on earth and often called a living fossil.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Okinawa (Naha)
days.summary: Shuri Castle, seat of the independent Ryukyu Kingdom for four centuries before Japan absorbed it, reflects a distinct culture, cuisine and even language found nowhere else in the country.
days.label: Early morning to afternoon

days.title: Ishigaki
days.summary: Manta rays glide through cleaning stations off this Yaeyama Islands hub in numbers rare anywhere else in Japan, drawing serious divers from around the world for a close encounter most only see on film.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Hong Kong
days.summary: Glide into Victoria Harbour as the skyline ignites, SeaDream III overnights here, so the Symphony of Lights becomes your private nightcap from the deck.
days.label: Evening, overnight

days.summary: A quiet Malaysian state capital on the South China Sea coast, known well beyond its size for a genuinely excellent Malay dining scene, keropok lekor fish crackers and nasi dagang among the local specialties worth seeking out at the waterfront night market.

days.summary: Trade the tide for the tropics of the Malaysian capital. The Perhentians are the stuff of desert-island dreams, turquoise water so clear the coral reads like a map, and no room for large ships in their shallow bays.

days.summary: Almost no cruise ship reaches the Anambas, a scattering of jewel-like islands adrift in the South China Sea, routinely ranked among Asia's most beautiful and least visited.

days.title: Parai Tenggiri
days.summary: Granite boulders, the same striking formations that made neighboring Belitung famous, line this quieter beach on Bangka Island, long overshadowed by its more photogenic neighbor.
days.label: Morning to late evening

days.title: Belitung
days.summary: Granite boulders the size of houses tumble straight into turquoise water along Belitung's coastline, a landscape made famous well beyond Indonesia by the bestselling novel and film Laskar Pelangi, both set on this small tin-mining island.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Krakatoa
days.summary: Few places on earth carry a name as loaded with history, the 1883 eruption here was heard nearly three thousand miles away and killed tens of thousands in the tsunamis it triggered, one of the deadliest natural disasters ever recorded.
days.label: Afternoon to evening

days.title: Ujung Kulon NP (Peucang Island)
days.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage rainforest at the far southwestern tip of Java, and the last refuge on earth of the critically endangered Javan rhinoceros, fewer than a hundred survive, all within this one park.
days.label: Early morning to evening

days.title: Thousand Islands (Pulau Seribu)
days.summary: Just off frenetic Jakarta lies its antidote: the Thousand Islands, a scatter of palm-topped coral cays within a national marine park.
days.label: Morning, overnight

days.title: Thousand Islands (Pulau Seribu) and Jakarta
days.summary: Just off frenetic Jakarta lies its antidote: the Thousand Islands, a scatter of palm-topped coral cays within a national marine park. Indonesia's electric capital rewards the intrepid.
days.label: Until early morning; Morning to afternoon

days.title: Semarang (Borobudur)
days.summary: Semarang is your gateway to Borobudur, the largest Buddhist monument on Earth: a mountain of grey volcanic stone crowned with bell-shaped stupas, best met at sunrise as mist lifts off the Kedu plain and 500 serene Buddhas emerge from the haze.
days.label: Morning, overnight

days.title: Semarang (Borobudur)
days.summary: Semarang is your gateway to Borobudur, the largest Buddhist monument on Earth: a mountain of grey volcanic stone crowned with bell-shaped stupas, best met at sunrise as mist lifts off the Kedu plain and 500 serene Buddhas emerge from the haze.
days.label: Until late evening

days.title: Karimunjawa
days.summary: A cluster of twenty-seven small islands scattered across the Java Sea, protected as a national marine park and rewarding anyone who makes the crossing with some of the clearest water and healthiest coral in the region.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Bawean Island
days.summary: A small volcanic island adrift in the Java Sea, home to the critically endangered Bawean deer, found nowhere else on the planet and rarely seen even here.
days.label: Morning to late evening

days.title: Surabaya
days.summary: Indonesia's second city wears its role in the independence struggle openly, the Heroes Monument commemorates the fierce 1945 battle that gave the country's National Heroes Day its name.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Probolinggo (Mount Bromo)
days.summary: The gateway to one of Indonesia's most photographed landscapes, Mount Bromo's smoking crater rises from a sea of volcanic sand inside the vast Tengger Caldera, best seen at dawn from the Penanjakan viewpoint as the sun clears the surrounding peaks.
days.label: Early morning to evening

days.title: Celukan Bawang
days.summary: The quieter gateway to North Bali, well removed from the crowds of Kuta and Seminyak, Celukan Bawang opens onto the Buleleng coast's black-sand beaches, waterfalls at Gitgit and Sekumpul, and dolphin pods that surface reliably off Lovina each morning.
days.label: Morning to late evening

days.title: Benoa (Bali)
days.summary: Benoa opens the whole of Bali to you. Watch the sun drop behind the sea-cliff temple of Uluwatu as barefoot dancers stamp out the hypnotic Kecak fire ritual, or rise early for the mirror-calm Tegallalang rice terraces above Ubud.
days.label: Arrives morning, disembark 8 AM to 10 AM

days.title: Lombok
days.summary: Bali's quieter neighbor rises to the volcanic cone of Mount Rinjani, Indonesia's second-highest peak, its crater lake a multi-day trek for the properly fit.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Satonda Island
days.summary: A tiny, uninhabited island off the north coast of Sumbawa hides a genuine geological oddity at its center, a saltwater crater lake, connected to the sea by seepage rather than any visible channel, ringed by fossilized coral microbialites found in only a handful of places worldwide.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Larantuka (Flores)
days.summary: A small Catholic town on Flores's eastern tip that holds one of Asia's most extraordinary religious traditions, a centuries-old Holy Week procession, rooted in 16th-century Portuguese missionary heritage, that still draws pilgrims from across the region each Easter.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Kupang
days.summary: West Timor's capital looks and feels different from the rest of Indonesia, a largely Christian city on the edge of a Muslim-majority nation, its markets built around lontar palm sugar and handwoven ikat rather than batik.
days.label: Morning to afternoon

days.title: Dili
days.summary: Dili wears its history openly: Portuguese pastel facades, the soaring Cristo Rei statue watching over the bay, and museums that tell Timor-Leste's hard- won independence.
days.label: Morning, overnight

days.title: Dili and Atauro Island
days.summary: Dili wears its history openly: Portuguese pastel facades, the soaring Cristo Rei statue watching over the bay, and museums that tell Timor-Leste's hard- won independence. A short but rough crossing from Dili delivers some of the most biodiverse reef in the world, surveys here have recorded more fish species per site than almost anywhere else on the planet.
days.label: Until early morning; Morning to evening

days.title: Darwin
days.summary: Australia's tropical northern capital carries its Second World War history openly, this was the only Australian city bombed by Japan, in a 1942 raid larger than Pearl Harbor, told in full at the wartime tunnels beneath town.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Seven Spirit Bay
days.place: Seven Spirit Bay, Northern Territory, Australia
days.summary: A genuinely wild stretch of the Cobourg Peninsula in western Arnhem Land, reachable only by boat or light aircraft and home to one of Australia's original ecotourism retreats.
days.label: Morning to late evening

days.title: Wessel Islands and Yirrkala
days.summary: A remote, largely uninhabited chain off the tip of Arnhem Land that carries evidence of Australia's first real contact with the outside world, Macassan fishermen from what is now Indonesia sailed here to harvest sea cucumber centuries before European settlement, leaving tamarind trees and pottery shards still being found today. This small Arnhem Land community changed Australian law from its own church hall, the 1963 bark petitions presented here, painted testimony backed by written text, were the first Indigenous documents recognized by the Australian Parliament and remain a founding document of the land rights movement.
days.label: Early morning to afternoon; Late evening, overnight

days.title: Yirrkala
days.summary: This small Arnhem Land community changed Australian law from its own church hall, the 1963 bark petitions presented here, painted testimony backed by written text, were the first Indigenous documents recognized by the Australian Parliament and remain a founding document of the land rights movement.
days.label: Until evening

days.summary: Where the Coral Sea meets the Arafura, tiny TI is the beating heart of the Torres Strait.

days.title: Townsville
days.summary: North Queensland's largest city looks out toward Magnetic Island and, further offshore, the Museum of Underwater Art, submerged sculptures designed to grow into a living reef of their own.
days.label: Morning to evening

days.title: Nara Inlet
days.summary: One of the Whitsundays' most sheltered anchorages doubles as one of its most significant cultural sites, a cave deep in the inlet holds ochre rock art left by the Ngaro people, sea-going Aboriginal navigators who called these waters home for thousands of years before European contact.
days.label: Morning to late evening

days.title: Airlie Beach
days.summary: The gateway to seventy-four islands of the Whitsundays, Airlie Beach trades any real waterfront for a lively strip of restaurants and a purpose-built lagoon pool, then sends everyone straight back out onto the water.
days.label: Early morning to late evening

days.title: Percy Islands
days.summary: One of the most remote anchorages on the Queensland coast, better known to generations of cruising sailors than to any tour operator.
days.label: Morning to late evening

days.title: Great Keppel Island
days.summary: Seventeen white-sand beaches ring this Keppel Bay island, most of them empty even on a busy day, backed by coastal woodland thick with birdlife.
days.label: Early morning to late evening

days.title: Lady Elliot Island
